modules.name: Program Value Study
modules.design_question: What is each tagged use worth per m2 in downtown Vancouver now, how deep is the market for the area supplied (office and strata), and how fresh is each number?
modules.effort: M-L: 6-7 person-days (evidence ledger, load factors, lease-up inputs, five use cards, freshness logic); quarterly data refresh
inputs: Layer 0: GFA by use and floor (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public)
P08-M02 NetAreaByUse (usable area per use)
Rentable/usable load factor per use and strata saleable-area definition (team assumptions, blank until entered)
Market-evidence ledger (editable rows: value, unit, net/gross, class, geography, date, source_id)
VTC brief (P08-S39): site 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2; 9.0 FSR non-residential = 103,213 m2 GFA (about 1.11 M sf), computed from the brief
Leasing-cost, lease-up and presale rows (TI, LC, free rent, units per month; team assumptions)
outputs: ValueByUse (typed table: use, rentable or saleable area, rent or price basis, vacancy, NOI, capitalised value, low/base/high, source_id, date, net/gross tag)
MarketDepth (office GFA / downtown AAA+A building area; years to lease; strata years to sell)
LeaseUpSchedule (pre-let, absorption path, TI, LC, free rent, vacancy carry) for P08-M05a
EvidenceFreshness (per-row age flag consumed by P08-M08)

parameters.name: Office net asking rent by class
parameters.relationship: Office NOI and capitalised value rise in proportion to net rent. Downtown Q2 2026 net asking spans $24.03 (C) to $48.02 (AAA), so the class the floors can credibly claim (plate, core, amenity) is a first-order value lever.

parameters.name: Taxes and operating costs (T&O) and net/gross tag
parameters.relationship: Tenant gross occupancy cost = net rent + T&O (AAA $26.13). NOI uses net rent only, so mixing net and gross numbers shifts value by roughly the T&O amount; every ledger value is tagged net or gross.

parameters.name: Rentable/usable load factor
parameters.relationship: Income area = GFA x NTG x (1 + load factor). Ilgin's efficiency is usable/gross but brokers quote rentable sf, so omitting the load understates income and undervalues efficient plates. No sourced value; BOMA standard not opened.

parameters.name: Stabilised vacancy and lease-up
parameters.relationship: Effective revenue falls one-for-one with vacancy; lease-up months and pre-let share set carry cost in M05a. Downtown Q2 2026: AAA 7.6%, A 9.1%, B 20.2%, so the AAA/A versus B/C split decides which rent tier is realistic.

parameters.name: Downtown net absorption
parameters.relationship: Years to lease = new GFA / net absorption, which caps how much office the market takes. Downtown H1 2026: +103,062 sf all classes (about 206,000 sf/yr), +128,448 AAA+A (derived). Leasing activity is gross deal flow, not absorption.

parameters.name: Leasing costs and incentives (TI, LC, free rent, T&O on vacant space)
parameters.relationship: Each cuts effective income and lengthens payback, so it raises the rent needed to pencil. BOMA BC reports high incentive packages without magnitudes; values are ranged team assumptions.

parameters.name: Residential tenure, price and rent
parameters.relationship: Strata revenue = saleable area x price; rental value = rent capitalised, so tenure choice shifts risk and charges. CMHC rents are existing-stock averages (condo vacancy 1.5%, purpose-built 3.7%); a new-build rent row is required.

parameters.name: Strata presale depth
parameters.relationship: Years to sell = units / presale absorption, and lender presale thresholds gate construction start, so unit count and mix are bounded by depth. Only signals found: Metro apartment benchmark -6.2% y/y and 11.4% sales-to-listings (secondary).

parameters.name: Hotel revenue and NOI
parameters.relationship: Total revenue = rooms revenue / rooms share, less departmental and undistributed costs, management fee and FF&E reserve. Vancouver 2025: 78.4% occupancy, ADR C$284.44, RevPAR C$223.05 (market undefined); brand tier is an ADR assumption; one tower hotel traded near C$1.0M/key.

parameters.name: Ground-floor retail net rent by frontage
parameters.relationship: Retail value scales with frontage quality, so which site edge carries retail matters: Robson 1000 block $180-240/sf net versus 1100 block $75-125 (Colliers, 2022), a 2-3x spread within two blocks. Data are stale.

parameters.name: Evidence age
parameters.relationship: Older evidence widens the range that P08-M08 applies to that input; the module flags any row older than the threshold (the retail evidence dates from 2022).

metrics.name: Evidence age (oldest ledger row)
metrics.basis: Benchmark: none. Cut-off: team assumption; broker series are quarterly and no source sets a staleness limit.
metrics.method: Today minus data date per ledger row; worst row shown with its source chip.

metrics.name: Office rent basis check
metrics.good: Class-matched downtown net asking rent (e.g. AAA $48.02/sf)
metrics.bad: Metro blended ($31.20) or Metro NNN ($46.81) used as downtown rent
metrics.basis: CBRE's $31.20 headline blends net and gross Metro-wide; Lee/CoStar's $46.81 is Metro NNN, all classes; CBRE downtown all-class net is $34.93. Benchmark verified (S01, S02). The rent ratio itself lives in M05a.
metrics.method: Badge fails if basis is gross or blended, geography is Metro, or class is unmatched.

metrics.name: Absorption load: new office GFA / downtown AAA+A building area
metrics.basis: CBRE inventory is gross building area (drip line), so GFA, not net area, is compared. Inventory 16,571,572 sf verified; cut-offs are team assumptions. Example: 70% of 9.0 FSR as office = 777,700 sf = 4.7%.
metrics.method: Office GFA from Layer 0 / 16.57 M sf; net-area variant shown as secondary.

metrics.name: Years of net absorption to lease the new office area
metrics.basis: Gross leasing activity removed as an upside (it is not net absorption). Anchor verified: H1 2026 annualised 206,124 sf/yr; example 777,700 / 206,124 = 3.8 years. Multipliers and cut-offs are team assumptions.
metrics.method: New GFA / annualised net absorption; low, base, high = 0.5x, 1x, 2x the anchor (editable) or a user-loaded multi-year series; deal flow shown separately.

metrics.name: Strata years to sell (presale basis)
metrics.basis: No sourced presale series or lender threshold; the user enters units per month and presale %.
metrics.method: Strata units / (presale units per month x 12); unsold inventory shown beside it.

modules.method: Read GFA by use and floor from Layer 0 and usable areas from P08-M02. For each use pull the matching ledger row (value, unit, net/gross, class, geography, date, source) and convert units. Income area = GFA x NTG x (1 + load factor). Office: NOI = rentable area x net rent x (1 - vacancy) - non-recoverables; lease-up path, TI, LC and free rent go to P08-M05a. Hotel: total revenue from rooms share, less costs, management fee and FF&E reserve. Retail: area x net rent by frontage. Strata: saleable area x user price (no default) with presale years-to-sell. Capitalise with an editable cap rate. Market depth: new office GFA against CBRE building area; years to lease from net absorption. Every figure carries a source chip; unsourced values show as editable team assumptions.
visualization: Stacked bar of value per m2 GFA by use with low/base/high whiskers; each segment carries a source chip (id, publisher, date, net/gross, class) and a freshness colour (green <= 6 months, amber 6-12, red > 12)
Market-depth gauges: new office GFA as a share of AAA+A building area, and years to lease against the CBRE four-year no-new-supply horizon; separate strata years-to-sell bar
Evidence table; rows corrected as FALSE ASSUMPTION struck through in the special colour with the correction beside them
modules.human_judgment: Which office class the design can credibly claim; rental versus strata; hotel tier; which edge carries retail; defensible low/base/high ranges; how to read broker disagreement (downtown vacancy 12.2% CBRE vs Vancouver 9.5% Colliers); presale and pre-let strategy.
modules.limits: Asking, not effective, rents (incentives unquantified); CBRE, Colliers and Lee/CoStar use different building sets; no sourced 2026 new-build strata price, presale series, cap rate or current retail rent; no transaction evidence for the hypothetical site.

modules.name: Floor-Plate Efficiency and Core Ratio
modules.design_question: How much of each floor's gross area is lettable or saleable, how much is core and circulation, and how does that efficiency erode as the tower gets taller?
modules.effort: M: 3-4 person-days (floor slicing, tag logic, benchmark overlay)
inputs: Layer 0: floor-by-floor slab outlines and storey count
Layer 0 tags: core, mechanical, program use per floor
Optional ADVANCED: structure system and vertical-transport core size (from the SYST packet)
outputs: FloorEfficiencyTable (per floor: GFA, core area, usable area, core ratio, NTG)
NetAreaByUse (usable basis; consumed by P08-M01 and M03)
BenchmarkFlags (NTG and core ratio against published tower samples)

parameters.name: Tower height / number of storeys
parameters.relationship: Across 166 towers height correlates negatively with space efficiency (Ilgin 2025): more lift banks, shafts and structure per floor, so extra height costs net area. The abstract gives no slope.

parameters.name: Core-to-GFA ratio
parameters.relationship: Net area = GFA minus core minus other non-lettable area, so each extra point of core removes about one point of NTG; core size is a plan decision. Samples: 11-38% (mean 26%, tapered supertall), 13-34% (mean 23%, Japan).

parameters.name: Structural system
parameters.relationship: Not used as a lever. The 166-tower abstract reports rigid frames near 85% NTG without height control; the tapered supertall sample (outriggered frames prevailing) found no significant effect of load-bearing system. Left unresolved until STRC supplies plausible systems.

parameters.name: Program mix and stacking
parameters.relationship: Hotel towers show the highest efficiency (mean 81.2%, 166 towers), so shifting hotel, residential and office shares changes blended efficiency and therefore the stacking choice.

parameters.name: Floor-plate area and depth
parameters.relationship: Unresolved: no sourced relationship between plate size or depth and core share for 244-305 m mixed-use towers; the module only measures it (see unresolved_relationships).

parameters.name: Area basis (usable vs rentable)
parameters.relationship: This module reports usable area. Broker rents and BOMA-type measures use rentable area with a common-area load, applied in P08-M01; mixing bases misstates income, so tagging common space drives value.

metrics.name: Net-to-gross ratio (whole tower)
metrics.basis: Benchmark verified: 40 Japanese tall buildings, mean 75%, range 64-85% (S19); 40 tapered supertalls, mean 72%, 55-84% (S17). Cut-offs are team picks from sample statistics, not a code limit.
metrics.method: Sum of usable area / sum of GFA across floors; per-use values also shown.

metrics.name: Core-to-GFA ratio (whole tower)
metrics.basis: Benchmark verified: Japanese sample mean 23%, maximum 34% (S19); tapered supertall mean 26%, maximum 38% (S17). Cut-offs are team picks from sample statistics.
metrics.method: Sum of core and mechanical-tagged area / sum of GFA.

metrics.name: Efficiency change per 10 storeys
metrics.basis: Only the direction (negative) is sourced (Ilgin 2025); displayed for the user's own tower, not judged.
metrics.method: Linear fit of per-floor NTG against floor number.

modules.method: Slice the Layer 0 model at each floor (mesh sections or IFC slab outlines) and compute slab GFA. Sum polygons tagged core, mechanical or refuge for core area; core ratio = core / GFA. Usable area = GFA minus tagged non-lettable areas (lobbies, mechanical, circulation if tagged); an editable envelope and circulation deduction (default none) is applied, with a warning that untagged circulation and wall thickness make a tagged-only result optimistic. Compute efficiency per floor, per use block and blended; compare with sample benchmarks. In ADVANCED mode replace the tagged core with the lift-core size from the SYST packet. Output NetAreaByUse (usable basis) for M01 and M03.
visualization: Tower section/elevation with each floor filled by NTG on a diverging scale (red < 64%, white 75%, blue >= 85%) beside a bar chart of core % per floor
Benchmark strip: the user's tower as a marker over the 55-84% (supertall) and 64-85% (Japanese) sample ranges, labelled 'sample range, not a code limit'
modules.human_judgment: Which spaces count as core versus lettable (sky lobbies, refuge floors, amenity); how much efficiency to trade for public-facing vertical uses and design quality.
modules.limits: Benchmarks come from published tower samples (Japan, global, tapered) with differing definitions; no Vancouver sample; plate-size relationship not quantified; usable-to-rentable load and by-law floor area (FSR) are handled in M01 and M06, not here.

modules.name: Construction Cost and Tall-Building Premium
modules.design_question: What will this massing cost to build by use and height in Vancouver today, how much of that is the tall-building premium, and how wide is the schematic-stage range?
modules.effort: M: 4-5 person-days (per-use cost ledger, building-level premium, AACE range logic)
inputs: Layer 0: GFA by use and floor including below-grade; storey count per use block
P08-M02 NetAreaByUse
Per-use base hard-cost ledger (value, unit, storey band, vintage; editable; blank where unsourced)
Escalation index to the valuation date (optional; default none)
ADVANCED presets: structural system, facade, MEP, vertical transport; AACE maturity checklist answers
outputs: HardCost (CAD, low/base/high) at building level, spread to floors by a labelled team-assumption profile
TotalDevelopmentCost excluding land and charges (hard + soft + contingency, range)
CostPremiumIndex (multiplier vs reference storeys)
CostEstimateClass (class and P10/P90 range) for P08-M05a and P08-M08

parameters.name: Base hard cost per use
parameters.relationship: Hard cost scales with area. Only residential concrete high-rise (13-39 storeys, $360-455/sf, hard cost only, Altus 2025) is sourced; office, hotel, retail, parking and the transit link stay blank until sourced, so use mix changes how much is assumed.

parameters.name: Number of storeys (building)
parameters.relationship: Average cost per m2 of a whole building rises with its floor count: elasticity about 0.1 to nine floors, 0.25-0.26 commercial and 0.56 residential above; rule of thumb +2% per floor (UK, 1971). Larger at extreme heights.

parameters.name: Use blend (GFA share by use)
parameters.relationship: The building exponent blends commercial and residential elasticities by GFA share, with 0.56 as the upper bound. The paper does not estimate mixed-use buildings or where uses sit in the tower, so stacking order is not a cost lever here.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor height by use
parameters.relationship: Storeys follow from height: 244-305 m is about 55-75 storeys at 4.0-4.4 m (office) and 75-100 at 3.0-3.2 m (residential), pushing residential further past the 39-storey band where the 0.56 elasticity bites (arithmetic).

parameters.name: Imported steel and aluminum prices
parameters.relationship: U.S.-origin steel and aluminum price pressure feeds mechanical, electrical and envelope costs; Altus names development-charge and code changes as the largest viability swings, so envelope and MEP ambition carry price risk.

parameters.name: Design maturity (AACE estimate class)
parameters.relationship: Ranges are P10/P90 (80% interval after contingency): Class 5 -20/-30% to +30/+50%; Class 4 -10/-20% to +20/+30%; Class 3 -5/-15% to +10/+20%. Class follows deliverable maturity; complex projects can run 2-3x higher on the high side.

parameters.name: Soft-cost % and contingency %
parameters.relationship: Total cost rises in proportion to these add-ons; no sourced Vancouver percentages were found (editable team assumptions), so ambition and risk appetite show up here.

parameters.name: Valuation date and escalation
parameters.relationship: Costs default to today's money; an optional index escalates to the valuation date over a long supertall build. Altus says 2025 Vancouver costs fell and the 2025 guide reflects late-2024 pricing.

metrics.name: Building-level tall-building premium (N/N_ref)^eps_blend
metrics.basis: Elasticities verified (Ahlfeldt and Barr, S16) but applied once per building, not per floor. The 26-storey anchor (midpoint of the Altus 13-39 band) is a team assumption; +2%/floor gives +68%.
metrics.method: Premium = (N_building / N_ref)^eps_blend, eps blended by GFA share; laws 0.26, 0.56 and 2%/floor shown as a range, not one answer.

metrics.name: Storeys above the Altus sampled band
metrics.basis: Altus 2025 band covers 13-39 storey concrete residential (S13); 244-305 m is roughly 55-100 storeys depending on floor height (arithmetic).
metrics.method: Max storeys per use block minus 39.

metrics.name: Applied cost range vs AACE class justified by maturity
metrics.good: Applied P10/P90 at least as wide as the class justified by the deliverables checklist (default Class 5)
metrics.bad: Narrower than the justified class (false precision)
metrics.basis: Benchmark verified: RP 56R-08 Table 1 (80% interval; class set by deliverable maturity, not percent). Table 3 checklist is absent from the opened sample, so a simplified three-question check is a team assumption.
metrics.method: Class from the maturity check; compare the applied range with Table 1; supertall extrapolation stays Class 5.

metrics.name: Share of GFA with a sourced base hard cost
metrics.basis: Benchmark: none. Only residential concrete is sourced today, so this shows how much of the estimate rests on team assumptions. Cut-offs are editable.
metrics.method: GFA of uses with a sourced ledger row / total GFA.

modules.method: Base cost per use comes from the ledger (blank where unsourced; Altus 2025 residential concrete $360-455/sf at N_ref = 26 is the only default). Building premium = (N / N_ref)^eps_blend applied once to the whole building: eps 0.1 up to 9 floors, then 0.26 commercial or 0.56 residential blended by GFA share; show 0.26, 0.56 and 2%-per-floor laws as a spread. Distribute cost to floors with a separate labelled team-assumption profile (the source does not measure it). Add a below-grade multiplier, soft cost % and contingency (unsourced) and optional escalation to the valuation date, then apply the AACE range (default Class 5; Class 4 only if the maturity check passes) as P10/P90. Flag storeys above 39. Example: 26 to 60 storeys gives x1.24 (0.26), x1.60 (0.56), x1.34 (70/30 blend).
visualization: Column per floor along the tower height (base + premium + soft + contingency) with a shaded P10-P90 envelope; the floor profile is labelled team assumption
Shaded box marking the Altus 13-39-storey band; storeys above it hatched 'extrapolated'
Three lines for the premium laws (0.26, 0.56, 2%/floor) so their spread reads as uncertainty; AACE class badge linked to the 56R-08 matrix
modules.human_judgment: Structural, facade and MEP ambition; contractor risk appetite; whether an iconic height premium is worth it against the jury's warning on unnecessarily expensive design.
modules.limits: Altus 2026 Vancouver tables are gated and not retrieved; the elasticities come from a global (Emporis) sample with 85% of costs missing and heights below supertall; office, hotel, retail, parking and transit-link costs are unsourced.

modules.name: Statutory Charges: ACC, DCL and DCC
modules.design_question: Which statutory levies (ACC, City DCL and Utilities DCL, Metro Vancouver and TransLink DCCs) would this scheme pay, when, and how large are they on a chosen valuation date?
modules.effort: S-M: 3 person-days (charges ledger, regime and date switch, deferral timing)
inputs: Layer 0: GFA by use, apartment unit count, tenure (rental or strata), site area
Valuation / application date (drives every rate, phase-in and escalator)
Rental class and eligibility toggles (Class A, Class B, none)
Charges ledger (rate, basis, effective date, status proposed/approved/in force, source_id)
outputs: ChargesSchedule (item, basis, CAD/sf, CAD total, effective date, status, source_id)
ChargesCashflow (payment timing including ACC and DCL deferral) for P08-M05a
ACCCreditOption (value if credited against a negotiated CAC) for P08-M05b

parameters.name: Amenity Cost Charge (ACC) by use
parameters.relationship: Proportional to floor area by use, so use mix and unit count change the bill. Applications after 30 Sep 2026: commercial/other $3.00/sf; apartments above 1.5 FSR $10.00 (50% in year one); +3%/yr 2027-29. Council approval 21 Jul 2026 per City summary; Table 1 unopened.

parameters.name: City DCL and Utilities DCL with 20% reduction
parameters.relationship: Proportional to area by use. After the 20% cut, residential-type rates are City-wide $49.88/m2 and Utilities $39.06/m2 (blog); commercial rates not retrieved. Reduction kept in the July 2026 update; DCLs over $500,000 can be deferred.

parameters.name: Metro Vancouver DCCs (sewer, water, parkland)
parameters.relationship: Proportional to area or units and fixed at building permit, so unit count matters. In force from 24 Jul 2026; from 1 Jan 2027 non-residential $5.83 + $7.51 + $0.60 = $13.94/sf; apartments $6,930 + $9,630 + $763 = $17,323/unit.

parameters.name: TransLink regional transportation DCC
parameters.relationship: Region-wide charge by use. From 1 Jan 2026: apartment $1,774/unit; non-residential about $1.16 (office) to $1.44 (retail) per sf, read from a Langley schedule (column assignment inferred), so office-heavy schemes pay less per sf than retail.

parameters.name: Rental relief by class
parameters.relationship: Staff proposal: ACC and DCL waiver 100% for Class A (20% below-market area), 86% for Class B (CMHC average rents); Utilities DCL always payable. DCL relief lists a site under 8,000 m2 and ends 15 Dec 2027; this block is 11,468 m2.

parameters.name: Deferral and payment timing
parameters.relationship: With DCLs of at least $500,000, 25% of ACC and DCL is paid before building permit; the rest is secured and paid before occupancy or within four years. Deferral moves cash out of early financing and shifts phasing choices.

parameters.name: Public art contribution
parameters.relationship: The standalone public-art policy ends for rezonings submitted after 30 Sep 2026; art is funded through the ACC, so no separate line applies, but on-site art can still be offered in kind.

metrics.name: Regime applied
metrics.good: ACC + DCL + DCC (plus negotiated CAC for a large complex rezoning) for an application after 30 Sep 2026
metrics.bad: Legacy per-sf CAC targets applied to a new rezoning
metrics.basis: CAC targets are removed for applications after 30 Sep 2026; CACs remain negotiated for larger, complex projects (Daily Hive 9 Jul 2026; City bulletin not opened).
metrics.method: Switch on application date; legacy rows struck through in the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour.

metrics.name: Rental relief eligibility check
metrics.bad: Any condition fails (e.g. site over 8,000 m2)
metrics.basis: Corrects 'rental exempt': relief is conditional (proposal S23; DCL programme conditions in S27 include site under 8,000 m2, nine storeys or more, CD-1 rezoning). Joint application of the conditions is not verified.
metrics.method: Test site area, storeys, tenure and class against the ledger conditions; show the Utilities DCL as payable.

metrics.name: Charge-rate status by line
metrics.good: Every line in force or approved with an opened source
metrics.bad: Any line proposed, inferred or unsourced (flagged)
metrics.basis: Benchmark: none. Counts ledger lines by status (in force, approved, proposed, inferred) so unverified rates stay visible on the board; the rule is a team choice.
metrics.method: Count lines per status and list the weakest.

metrics.name: Total charges per m2 GFA (ACC + DCL + DCC)
metrics.basis: No source sets an acceptable level. Example, non-residential from 1 Jan 2027 excluding the City DCL (not retrieved): $3.00 + $13.94 + $1.16-1.44 = about $18.1-18.4/sf.
metrics.method: Sum of schedule lines / GFA.

modules.method: ACC = sum over uses of area (sf) x rate x phase-in(date) x escalator: commercial/other $3.00; apartments above 1.5 FSR $10.00 (50% until 30 Sep 2027); 3% a year on 30 Sep 2027-29; rental relief by class. City DCL and Utilities DCL = area x ledger rate (x 0.8 where the 20% reduction is not already in the rate; commercial rates missing). Metro Vancouver DCCs and TransLink DCC = area or units x the rate in force on the date each is set (building permit). Each row carries a status (proposed, approved, in force). Deferral: 25% of ACC and DCL at permit, remainder at occupancy or four years. Output a dated schedule; a regime toggle strikes through legacy rows. Land lift and CAC are computed in P08-M05b, which removes the M04/M05 loop.
visualization: Stacked bars of charges per m2 GFA by use (ACC, DCL, Utilities DCL, Metro DCCs, TransLink), each segment with a status chip (in force, approved, proposed, inferred)
Effective-date timeline: 24 Jul 2026 and 1 Jan 2027 (DCC steps), 30 Sep 2026 (ACC), 30 Sep 2027-29 (phase-in, +3%); legacy rows in the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour
Toggle between ACC regime and legacy regime; rental-class selector showing the waiver and the Utilities DCL still payable
modules.human_judgment: Which application date to assume; rental class and whether to seek relief; how hotel and cultural/civic floors are classed; whether to model a justified policy breach (the brief says the jury may reward one); Nation partnership terms are not monetised.
modules.limits: City ACC bulletin, Council report and DCL pages returned HTTP 403: ACC Table 1 and commercial DCL rates unopened; approval date rests on a City summary seen in search results; TransLink column assignment inferred; policy may change after the Higher Buildings review.

modules.name: Pro Forma and Residual Land Value before CAC
modules.design_question: At today's rents, costs and statutory charges, does this massing support a competitive return and a positive residual land value before any negotiated CAC, and what rent or price would it need to break even?
modules.effort: L: 6-7 person-days (two modes, lease-up, cash flow, break-even solver, export)
inputs: P08-M01 ValueByUse and LeaseUpSchedule
P08-M03 TotalDevelopmentCost range and CostEstimateClass
P08-M04 ChargesSchedule and ChargesCashflow
P08-M06 PublicFloorAdjustment and extra capex (optional; zero if M06 is not attached)
User rows: land benchmark, acquisition costs, land finance, build duration, financing rate, cap rates, disposal and purchaser's costs, GST treatment, valuation date
outputs: RLV_preCAC (point value; P10/P50/P90 only via P08-M08, no feedback)
ProfitOnGDV, ProfitOnCost, YieldOnCost, DevelopmentSpread
BreakEvenRentByUse (rent or price that gives RLV = benchmark)
CapValueCrossCheck; RLV_preCAC by use for proposed and baseline zoning (to P08-M05b)

parameters.name: Gross development value (GDV) and cap rate
parameters.relationship: RLV rises one-for-one with GDV; income value is proportional to 1 / cap rate, so +50 bp on 4.72% cuts office value about 10%. 4.72% is CoStar's Metro office figure (Q2 2026), not tower-grade evidence, so use mix decides exposure.

parameters.name: Total development cost
parameters.relationship: RLV falls one-for-one with cost. CBRE states that economic rents for new downtown office are significantly higher than market rents, with no new supply for at least four years from construction start, so office share is the binding choice.

parameters.name: Developer return
parameters.relationship: A higher required return deducts more from GDV before land. UK planning guidance treats 15-20% of GDV as suitable for plan-making; a transferable convention, not Vancouver policy.

parameters.name: Land benchmark value
parameters.relationship: RLV must exceed existing-use value plus a landowner premium for a sale (UK PPG paras 014-017 convention). The hypothetical VTC site has no price, so the user sets the benchmark.

parameters.name: Land acquisition cost and land carry
parameters.relationship: Property transfer tax (1% to $200k, 2% to $2M, 3% above; about 3% on a large site) plus legal fees and land interest enlarge the land outlay, so RLV = residual / (1 + a + f). Legal and carry are assumptions.

parameters.name: Disposal costs, purchaser's costs and GST
parameters.relationship: Income assets sell net of selling costs and the buyer's transfer tax, lowering GDV; strata revenue is net of selling costs, with GST treated as pass-through. First-time buyer GST rebate (up to $50,000, homes under $1.5M) is buyer-specific.

parameters.name: Lease-up and leasing costs
parameters.relationship: Stabilised value arrives only after lease-up; vacancy carry, TI, commissions and free rent are discounted at the finance rate and deducted from GDV, so pre-let share and phasing change the result. Values are team assumptions.

parameters.name: Build duration and financing rate
parameters.relationship: Interest carry grows with duration and rate; taller towers plausibly take longer, but no sourced Vancouver tall-tower schedule or rate was found (editable team assumptions), so height choices are penalised only through these inputs.

parameters.name: Public floor area and contributions
parameters.relationship: ACC, DCL and DCC reduce RLV one-for-one; non-revenue public floors (M06) reduce GDV. The negotiated CAC is deducted only in M05b, so lift is not measured on an RLV already net of CAC.

parameters.name: Valuation date and escalation
parameters.relationship: Costs, rents and charges run from one valuation date; default is today's money with charges at the application-date rate (ACC +3%/yr 2027-29; Metro DCC step 1 Jan 2027), so build-period timing is explicit.

metrics.name: Profit on GDV (land at benchmark, with acquisition and land finance)
metrics.basis: Benchmark: transferable (UK PPG para 019, 15-20% for plan-making; alternative figures allowed; Vancouver practice unverified). Cut-off: team assumption.
metrics.method: Profit mode: (GDV - TDC excl. land - L_b x (1 + a + f)) / GDV.

metrics.name: Residual land value vs benchmark (before CAC)
metrics.basis: Benchmark: transferable (UK PPG paras 014-017: existing-use value plus premium); between the two is marginal. Cut-offs: team assumption.
metrics.method: Residual mode: RLV = (GDV - TDC excl. land - r x GDV) / (1 + a + f), divided by the user benchmark.

metrics.name: Break-even office net rent / class-matched CBRE downtown asking (AAA $48.02)
metrics.basis: Benchmark verified (CBRE Q2 2026, S01); cut-offs are editable presets. CBRE says new-build economic rents exceed market. This is the packet's only rent-ratio metric (M01 keeps the basis check).
metrics.method: Root-find the net rent that gives RLV = benchmark; divide by the CBRE row for the chosen class.

metrics.name: Development spread (yield on cost minus cap rate)
metrics.basis: Unsourced rule of thumb, editable; reference cap rate 4.72% is CoStar Metro modelled, not tower evidence (S02).
metrics.method: Stabilised NOI / TDC (incl. land) minus cap rate.

metrics.name: Capitalised value per sf / recent trade price per sf
metrics.basis: Benchmark verified: Lee Q2 2026 Metro average sale $477/sf; trades $455-542/sf (mostly Class B). AAA example 48.02 x 92.4% / 4.72% = about $940/sf (2.0x). Cut-offs: team assumption.
metrics.method: Capitalised value per rentable sf / trade evidence; also shown against full replacement cost per sf.

modules.method: Two explicit modes. Residual: RLV = (GDV - TDC excl. land - r x GDV) / (1 + a + f), with a = acquisition cost % (transfer tax, legal) and f = land finance factor. Profit: Profit = GDV - [TDC excl. land + L_b x (1 + a + f)]. Hand check: GDV 1,000; TDC 700; r 15%; a 3%; f 5% gives RLV 138.9; profit mode at L_b = 138.9 returns 150 (15%). GDV = capitalised income (net rent x (1 - vacancy) - non-recoverables, less lease-up deductions, purchaser's and disposal costs) plus strata net of selling costs, GST as pass-through. TDC = hard + soft + contingency + M04 charges + construction finance from an S-curve (numpy-financial). Baseline-zoning RLV by use goes to M05b. Break-even by SciPy brentq. Unit-test both modes against the hand example.
visualization: Waterfall from GDV through costs, statutory charges and developer return to RLV before CAC, each bar linked to its module and source chip
Break-even bars per use against the market-evidence band, with the CBRE class asking rent as a vertical reference line
Traffic-light badges per metric that open the source clause; capitalised-value strip against trades and replacement cost
modules.human_judgment: Required return and risk premium; site land value; phasing and pre-sale strategy; whether a marginal result is acceptable for a deliberate policy breach or an ideas-competition scheme; how to read break-even rents against the market.
modules.limits: Arithmetic on uncertain inputs: no sourced 2026 strata price, hotel or tower cap rate; asking rents overstate effective rents; return and land-benchmark logic are UK conventions; single-phase only (multi-tower phasing not modelled); not a valuation opinion.

modules.name: Land Lift, Negotiated CAC and RLV after CAC
modules.design_question: How large is the land lift by use, how much negotiated CAC could a large rezoning be asked to share, and what residual land value remains after CAC and in-kind public floors?
modules.effort: S-M: 2-3 person-days (lift by use, CAC toggles, credit logic)
inputs: P08-M05a RLV_preCAC by use for proposed and baseline zoning (baseline entered by the user)
P08-M06 InKindBenefitValue
P08-M04 ACCCreditOption
CAC share of lift (0-80%; 75% legacy reference) and netting toggle
outputs: LandLiftByUse (residential, employment, total; may be negative)
CACEstimate (range; never below zero)
RLV_postCAC and PublicBenefitTotal (ACC + cash CAC + in-kind value) for P08-M07
FeasibilityFlag

parameters.name: Land lift by use
parameters.relationship: Lift = RLV_preCAC(proposed) - RLV(baseline), computed for residential and employment floors separately; office may show negative lift because CBRE says new office does not pencil at market rents, so use mix drives the CAC base.

parameters.name: CAC share of lift
parameters.relationship: CAC rises with lift, so a larger density request raises the ask. Legacy policy 1.2(c) targeted at least 75% (secondary quote); Lincoln Institute cites 70-80%. Targets are removed after 30 Sep 2026, but negotiated CACs remain for large projects; share is an input.

parameters.name: Netting rule and exemptions
parameters.relationship: CAC on residential lift only, or on net total lift. The staff proposal exempts 100% employment or institutional rezonings; how the City treats a mixed scheme is unverified. CAC never goes below zero, so employment share changes the base.

parameters.name: ACC credit against CAC
parameters.relationship: Projects with secured CAC obligations could receive ACC credits to avoid double charging; BC guidance bars Density Bonus for amenities already in an ACC by-law. Credit size is unverified, so it is a toggle.

parameters.name: In-kind public floors and valuation basis
parameters.relationship: In-kind floors are already deducted in M05a (foregone revenue, capex). Here they are added back to measure lift, then credited against the CAC, so they are not counted twice. How the City values in-kind amenities is unverified.

metrics.name: CAC as share of land lift (reference only)
metrics.basis: Policy 1.2(c) 75% is quoted by a secondary blog (primary not opened); Lincoln cites 70-80%. Survival for large rezonings after 30 Sep 2026 is unverified; 75% is a City target, not a good outcome.
metrics.method: (Cash CAC + in-kind value) / lift base chosen by the netting toggle.

metrics.name: In-kind benefit / CAC-equivalent (share x lift)
metrics.basis: Built on the unverified 75% and 70% references; shown as a scenario, not a compliance test. Needs lift from P08-M05a.
metrics.method: Value of public floors (foregone value or cost) / (CAC share x lift).

metrics.name: RLV after CAC vs benchmark
metrics.basis: Benchmark: transferable (UK PPG paras 014-017). Public benefit lowers RLV one-for-one; cut-offs: team assumption.
metrics.method: RLV_postCAC = RLV_preCAC - cash CAC (in-kind already deducted in M05a); divide by the user benchmark.

metrics.name: Lift sign check by use
metrics.good: Residential lift >= 0 and employment lift shown separately
metrics.basis: Benchmark: none; design rule from CBRE's economic-rent statement (S01). Whether the City nets lift across uses is unknown.
metrics.method: Flag any negative component; require an explicit netting choice.

modules.method: Run P08-M05a for the proposed zoning and for the baseline entitlement (user-entered), by use group. Lift for CAC = RLV_preCAC(proposed) + value of in-kind floors (added back as market floors) - RLV(baseline). CAC base = residential lift only, or net total lift (toggle). Obligation = share x base (0-80%; 75% shown as legacy reference). Cash CAC = max(0, obligation - in-kind value - ACC credit option). RLV_postCAC = RLV_preCAC - cash CAC, because in-kind floors are already deducted in M05a. PublicBenefitTotal = ACC + cash CAC + in-kind value for P08-M07. CAC flows only forward, so there is no loop with M04 or M05a.
visualization: Waterfall continuing M05a: RLV before CAC to cash CAC, in-kind credit and RLV after CAC, each bar with a source chip and status
Lift by use as paired bars (residential, employment) with the netting toggle shown; negative bars drawn below the axis
Toggle between ACC-credit on and off, and between CAC share presets (0, 70, 75, 80%)
modules.human_judgment: Whether to model a justified breach of policy (the brief says the jury may reward one); which in-kind amenities to offer instead of cash; realism of the negotiation; Nation partnership terms are not monetised.
modules.limits: CAC regime for large rezonings after 30 Sep 2026 is unverified; primary CAC policy, City bulletin and in-kind valuation rule not opened; baseline entitlement and land value are user inputs; policy may change after the Higher Buildings review.

modules.name: Public-Use Cost Ledger
modules.design_question: What does the public-facing, civic and cultural floor area cost the project in foregone revenue and extra build cost, and does the 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum still pencil?
inputs: Layer 0 tags: cultural/civic, public, amenity, retail; floor level of each public area
P08-M01 ValueByUse (rent of the displaced use)
P08-M03 cost per floor
By-law floor-area exclusion rules (below-grade, mechanical, permitted amenity; editable)
VTC brief (P08-S39): 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum; public-facing uses should extend vertically
outputs: PublicUseCostLedger (area, foregone NOI, extra capex, annualised cost, value foregone)
NonResidentialFSRCheck (pass/fail under two readings, on by-law floor area)
InKindBenefitValue (to P08-M05b and P08-M07); PublicFloorAdjustment (to P08-M05a)

parameters.name: Public floor area by level
parameters.relationship: Foregone NOI = area x net rent of the displaced use. Height rent premia vary: 0.03 commercial and 0.07 residential in cited US cities, 0.086-0.189 within US commercial buildings; the floor premium is editable, so where public floors sit changes foregone income.

parameters.name: Non-residential FSR
parameters.relationship: The brief lists at least 9.0 FSR non-residential (103,213 m2 on this site). A public floor that counts helps compliance but earns less than office, widening the rent gap CBRE describes.

parameters.name: By-law floor-area exclusions
parameters.relationship: FSR uses by-law floor area, not Layer 0 GFA; excluded areas (below-grade, mechanical, permitted amenity) can inflate a pass, so what is modelled as excluded decides compliance. Rules are editable; the by-law could not be opened.

parameters.name: Lease terms for public uses
parameters.relationship: Nominal or below-market rent raises foregone NOI toward the full market rent; no sourced Vancouver convention was found (editable team assumption), so the tenancy model is a design lever.

parameters.name: Valuation basis of in-kind amenities
parameters.relationship: Valuing at replacement cost versus foregone value changes the credited amount, so how each amenity is delivered changes its credit; the City's in-kind valuation rule could not be verified.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR achieved (by-law floor area)
metrics.basis: Brief summaries (S39) give a 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum; the brief PDF was not opened and the wording ('recommended'?) and counted uses are unconfirmed. Two readings shown; Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026.
metrics.method: By-law non-residential floor area / 11,468 m2 under (a) all non-residential and (b) office and commercial only.

metrics.name: Public-use cost as share of GDV
metrics.basis: No source sets an acceptable share; plotted in P08-M07.
metrics.method: Value foregone plus extra capex / GDV.

modules.method: For every floor with cultural/civic, public or amenity tags: foregone NOI = area x net rent of the displaced use (user picks office, retail or residential equivalent) x (1 - vacancy). Extra capex = editable premium for lifts, structure and ceiling height plus fit-out. Capitalise foregone NOI at the M05a cap rate to get value foregone. Check non-residential FSR = by-law non-residential floor area (after editable exclusion rules) / site area against 9.0 under two readings (all non-residential; office and commercial only). Illustrative split of the 9.0 FSR (team assumption): 70% office, 20% hotel, 10% retail = 72,249 / 20,643 / 10,321 m2. List non-monetised items (reconciliation, Indigenous partnership, cultural value) with no dollar figure.
visualization: Vertical section with public floors coloured by use and labelled with annual foregone NOI and extra capex
Side stacked bar splitting cost into foregone revenue and capex; progress bar for 9.0 FSR on by-law area with pass/fail badge linked to the brief clause
Non-monetised items drawn as hatched blocks with no dollar value
modules.human_judgment: What counts as public benefit and how it is valued; reconciliation and cultural value must not be monetised by the tool; the distribution of benefits and partnership terms with the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.
modules.limits: No sourced valuation rule for in-kind benefits; the brief is ambiguous on what counts toward the 9.0 minimum; by-law exclusions unopened; foregone-revenue logic assumes the space would otherwise be let at market; indirect benefits are not modelled.

modules.name: Density-Benefit-Feasibility Explorer
modules.design_question: Across height, density and public-benefit packages, where is the feasible zone, what does each added public benefit cost, and which options sit on the trade-off frontier?
modules.effort: L: 6-8 person-days (variant table, frontier, interactive views; parametric rule only if declared)
inputs: P08-M05a and P08-M05b outputs evaluated per forked Layer 0 variant (or per cell of a declared parametric rule)
P08-M06 public-benefit totals; P08-M04 charges
P08-M08 distributions (optional outer sampler)
Layer 0 variants (forked massing models) or the declared parametric scaling rule
outputs: FeasibilityGrid (profit on GDV, RLV minus benchmark, public benefit per variant or cell)
ParetoSet (non-dominated variants)
ShadowPriceOfBenefit (RLV lost per m2 or CAD of public benefit)
ScenarioCards (for boards and the policy reflection)

parameters.name: Total GFA / FSR (or storeys)
parameters.relationship: More density raises GDV, but average cost per m2 rises with building height (elasticity about 0.26 commercial, 0.56 residential), so profit per m2 can fall beyond some height; the feasible band is bounded. Each cell needs a regenerated massing.

parameters.name: Parametric scaling rule
parameters.relationship: Layer 0 is a fixed massing, so a sweep needs a rule: add or remove typical floors by use and re-derive core, NTG (M02) and cost (M03). The rule is a labelled team assumption and limits which designs are explored.

parameters.name: Public-benefit package size
parameters.relationship: Each CAD of CAC/ACC or each m2 of non-revenue floor lowers RLV one-for-one; the legacy 75% target ties the ask to land lift, so density that adds lift can fund more benefit (target unverified for new rezonings).

parameters.name: Use mix (office vs residential vs hotel)
parameters.relationship: Building-level residential cost grows faster with height than commercial (0.56 vs 0.26), while office rents sit below the level CBRE says new development needs; the mix decides which constraint binds.

parameters.name: Market and cost scenario
parameters.relationship: Shifting rents, costs or cap rates moves the feasible boundary; ranges come from P08-M08 when attached, otherwise from simple low/base/high toggles.

metrics.name: Feasible share of design space
metrics.basis: A variant is feasible when profit >= 15% and RLV >= benchmark (M05a cut-offs: transferable benchmark, team choice).
metrics.method: Count feasible variants or cells / all.

metrics.name: Probability that the chosen scenario is feasible
metrics.basis: Benchmark: none. Cut-offs are editable presets; no source sets a confidence level. Requires P08-M08.
metrics.method: Share of Monte Carlo draws meeting both thresholds.

metrics.name: Shadow price of public benefit
metrics.basis: Finite difference along the frontier; informs, does not judge.
metrics.method: Change in RLV / change in public floor area or contribution.

modules.method: Primary mode: evaluate a finite set of user-forked variants by calling P08-M01 to M06 as pure functions; record profit on GDV, RLV_postCAC minus benchmark and total public benefit; extract the non-dominated set with plain non-dominated sorting. Optional mode: a declared parametric generator (team-assumption scaling rule) feeds a grid over GFA or storeys and public-benefit share; mark feasible cells and draw contours. NSGA-II (pymoo) is reserved for that generator, not for forked variants. Shadow price = RLV change per extra unit of public benefit along the frontier. With P08-M08 attached, colour by probability of feasibility. The 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum (P08-S39) is drawn as a constraint.
visualization: Heat map (parametric mode): x = total FSR or storeys, y = public-benefit share, colour = profit on GDV (diverging, white at 15%), contours at profit 15% and RLV = benchmark; cells below 9.0 FSR non-residential hatched
Pareto scatter and parallel-coordinates plot of forked variants, brushed to highlight the frontier
Ternary plot of office/residential/hotel share coloured by RLV; line chart of shadow price along the frontier
modules.human_judgment: Which frontier point the team defends; weighting of the four jury criteria; whether a marginally infeasible but culturally strong scheme is acceptable in an ideas competition.
modules.limits: Only as good as inputs from M01 to M06; no Vancouver evidence on how public benefit passes through to land price; parametric mode depends on a team-assumption scaling rule; a low-dimensional grid can hide interactions; not a valuation opinion.

modules.name: Uncertainty and Sensitivity Engine
modules.design_question: How uncertain is each economic result, which inputs drive it, and what range should the boards show instead of a single number?
inputs: Parameter ranges from any module (low, base, high, distribution, source_id)
CostEstimateClass from P08-M03
EvidenceFreshness from P08-M01
Rent-definition spread rows (CBRE downtown class rents, Lee/CoStar Metro NNN)
outputs: P10/P50/P90 for RLV before and after CAC, profit on GDV, yield on cost
Probability of meeting each threshold
Driver ranking (Sobol indices, or Shapley effects and rank correlations when inputs are correlated)

parameters.name: Estimate class and cost range
parameters.relationship: AACE ranges are 80% intervals after contingency, so they set P10/P90, not min/max: Class 5 -20/-30% to +30/+50%; Class 4 -10/-20% to +20/+30%; Class 3 -5/-15% to +10/+20%. Design maturity narrows the cost spread.

parameters.name: Market-definition spread
parameters.relationship: Brokers differ on vacancy (CBRE downtown 12.2%, Colliers Vancouver 9.5%, Lee Metro 9.9%) and rent (CBRE downtown all-class net $34.93, AAA $48.02; Lee Metro NNN $46.81). Source choice is uncertainty, so the claimed class changes the range.

parameters.name: Distribution shape and draws
parameters.unit: lognormal or skewed triangular; N draws
parameters.relationship: Fit each input so its P10/P90 match the stated bounds instead of using bounds as min/max; JCGM 101 specifies Monte Carlo propagation. Shape is an editable team assumption that widens or narrows tails.

parameters.name: Input correlation
parameters.relationship: Correlated rent and cap-rate moves change the output range and invalidate Sobol indices; with correlation on, use Shapley effects or rank correlations. No sourced correlation exists (default none, flagged).

metrics.name: Probability profit on GDV >= 15%
metrics.basis: Benchmark: transferable (UK PPG para 019 15% line). Cut-offs are editable presets; no source sets a confidence level.
metrics.method: Share of draws with profit >= 15%.

metrics.name: Probability RLV >= land benchmark
metrics.basis: Benchmark: transferable (UK PPG paras 014-017). Cut-offs are editable presets.
metrics.method: Share of draws with RLV >= benchmark.

metrics.name: Sensitivity method validity
metrics.good: Sobol only with independent inputs; Shapley or rank correlation when correlated
metrics.bad: Sobol indices reported with correlated inputs
metrics.basis: SALib lists Sobol and Shapley effects (S51); whether its Shapley code accepts correlated inputs is not verified. Rule is a design choice.
metrics.method: Check the correlation matrix; switch method and show a warning.

modules.method: Every module parameter carries (low, base, high, distribution, source_id). Fit distributions so P10/P90 match the stated bounds: AACE class range for cost, broker spread and evidence age for rents and vacancy, editable team ranges elsewhere. Draw N Sobol quasi-random samples (scipy.stats.qmc), run P08-M01 to M05b as an outer wrapper that never feeds back, and report P10/P50/P90 and threshold probabilities following JCGM 101. Rank drivers with Sobol total-order indices when inputs are independent; with user-set correlations switch to Shapley effects (SALib) or rank correlations and show a warning. Add rent-definition spread rows to rent ranges. Cache results per scenario fork so P08-M07 can colour its grid.
visualization: Tornado chart of ranked driver indices; each bar labelled sourced, team assumption or FALSE ASSUMPTION by colour
Violin or fan chart of RLV with P10/P50/P90 whiskers and the benchmark as a reference line
Probability-of-feasibility gauge; range bars for market inputs drawn from the broker spread
modules.human_judgment: Choosing ranges and correlations; deciding which uncertainty is reducible by design; presenting ranges rather than point estimates on the boards.
modules.limits: Most distributions are team assumptions because few sources publish ranges; correlations are unmodelled by default; ranges reflect parameter uncertainty, not model-structure error; broker spreads reflect definitions as much as true uncertainty.

flags.claim: The Metro Vancouver average asking rent of $31.20/sf in CBRE's Q2 2026 headline is the downtown office rent.
flags.correction: Use class-matched downtown net asking rents: AAA $48.02, A $39.92, B $33.02, C $24.03 (all downtown classes $34.93).
flags.detail: CBRE defines the headline as a metro-wide average that blends net and gross lease rates; mixing bases misstates value by the T&O amount ($19.50-$26.13/sf downtown).

flags.claim: Legacy CAC targets (fixed per-sf targets for rezonings) apply to a new Vancouver rezoning.
flags.correction: For rezoning applications submitted after 30 Sep 2026, CAC targets are removed and the city-wide ACC applies (commercial $3.00/sf; apartments above 1.5 FSR $10.00/sf at 50% in year one); negotiated CACs remain for larger, complex projects.
flags.detail: From a 9 Jul 2026 press report and a HAVAN summary; the City bulletin and Council report returned HTTP 403, and the approval date is reported as 21 Jul by the City against a scheduled 14 Jul meeting.

flags.claim: The Altus 2025 Vancouver concrete high-rise band ($360-455/sf) can be applied unchanged to 244-305 m towers.
flags.correction: The band covers 13-39 storeys and hard cost only (no site servicing, consultants or development charges); apply a height-premium law and flag everything above 39 storeys as extrapolated.
flags.detail: 244-305 m is roughly 55-75 storeys at 4.0-4.4 m per floor (arithmetic); the 2026 Altus tables for Vancouver were not retrieved.

flags.claim: CBRE's five-year average quarterly leasing (about 518,000 sf) can serve as the upside for downtown net absorption when computing years to lease.
flags.correction: Use downtown net absorption (H1 2026 +103,062 sf all classes, about 206,000 sf/yr; AAA+A rows +128,448) with 0.5x/1x/2x team multipliers, and show leasing activity only as separate deal flow.
flags.detail: Leasing activity is gross deal volume including renewals and moves; CBRE defines net absorption as the change in occupied sf (S01, pp.3 and 5). The error implied about 0.4 years to lease 888,800 sf.

flags.claim: Rental developments are exempt from the ACC and from DCLs.
flags.correction: Relief is conditional: the ACC proposal gives a 100% waiver (Class A, 20% below-market area) or 86% (Class B, CMHC average rents); all rentals still pay the Utilities DCL; DCL relief has eligibility limits and runs to 15 Dec 2027.
flags.detail: Daily Hive 9 Jul 2026 (S23, pre-vote); McCarthy Tetrault (S27) lists conditions including a site under 8,000 m2, and this 11,468 m2 block exceeds it. Statutory exemptions cover only listed affordable classes (S44).

flags.claim: Ahlfeldt and Barr's height elasticities (0.26 commercial, 0.56 residential) are per-floor multipliers, and the stacking order of uses changes cost.
flags.correction: They are building-level elasticities of average cost per floor space on floor count. Apply (N/N_ref)^eps once per building with eps blended by GFA share; the stacking-order claim is removed.
flags.detail: Footnote 16 and Fig. 6 note (S16): log cost per floor space regressed on log floor count across buildings; costs missing for about 85% of Emporis buildings; larger at extreme heights (S40); 2%/floor is a 1971 UK rule.

flags.claim: AACE 56R-08 class ranges are hard bounds (or triangular min/max), and a design reaches Class 4 once ADVANCED presets are set.
flags.correction: Treat the ranges as P10/P90 (80% interval after contingency); assign class by deliverable maturity; default to Class 5 for BASIC massing and supertall extrapolation.
flags.detail: RP 56R-08 Table 1 and text (S21): maturity of deliverables is the sole determining characteristic of class; high ranges may be two to three times larger for complex or risky projects.

flags.claim: The CAC share threshold (at least 75% of land lift) is a verified good outcome.
flags.correction: It is an unverified secondary quote of policy 1.2(c); treat 75% as the City's legacy minimum target and display it as a reference, not a feasibility pass mark.
flags.detail: More Housing Substack quotes the policy (S28); the 70-80% figure comes via MacPhail, not policy. CAC targets are removed after 30 Sep 2026, so survival of 75% for large rezonings is unverified.

flags.claim: UK PPG para 019 verifies a 15% profit-on-GDV threshold for this project.
flags.correction: Status is team_assumption with a transferable benchmark: para 019 is plan-making guidance for England, allows alternative figures, and is not Vancouver practice or a site-specific test.
flags.detail: gov.uk viability guidance (S20): 15-20% of GDV may be a suitable return (revised 2019). Vancouver convention (Coriolis reports for the City) not opened.

flags.claim: A negotiated CAC applies to the whole land lift of this mixed-use rezoning.
flags.correction: Compute lift by use; offer toggles for CAC on residential lift versus net total lift; never allow a negative CAC; flag the exemption rule as unverified.
flags.detail: Daily Hive 9 Jul 2026 (S23): 100% employment or institutional rezonings are exempt from CAC negotiations; office may show negative lift (S01 economic-rent statement). City netting practice unknown.

flags.claim: CBRE downtown inventory (16.57 M sf AAA+A) is comparable to the tower's net lettable area.
flags.correction: Compare new building area (GFA) with CBRE building area; show net or rentable area only as a secondary variant.
flags.detail: CBRE definitions (S01 p.5): building area is the total floor area, typically taken at the drip line, a gross measure.

flags.claim: Lee/CoStar's Metro average NNN asking rent ($46.81/sf, Q2 2026) can be used as downtown office underwriting rent.
flags.correction: Use class-matched downtown net asking rents (CBRE AAA $48.02; all classes $34.93); an NNN figure without class and geography match fails the ledger check.
flags.detail: In the same quarter CBRE's downtown all-class net is $34.93, so $46.81 would overstate value by about a third (S01, S02).

flags.claim: Rigid-frame towers reaching about 85% net-to-gross show that structural system is an efficiency lever at 244-305 m.
flags.correction: Treat it as a sample correlation without height control; the tapered supertall sample found no significant system effect; leave the relationship unresolved until the STRC packet supplies plausible systems.
flags.detail: Abstracts (S17, S18): outriggered frames prevailed in the supertall sample and load-bearing system effects were not significant; the 166-tower abstract reports no height-controlled result.

flags.claim: The Altus 2025 residential concrete band can serve as base hard cost for every use (office, hotel, retail, parking, transit link).
flags.correction: Base cost is a per-use ledger: only residential concrete (13-39 storeys, $360-455/sf, hard cost only) is sourced; other uses stay blank or flagged team assumptions.
flags.detail: The 2025 guide extract (S13) gives no office, hotel, retail or parking figures; the 2026 tables are gated (S15).

flags.claim: Metro Vancouver water and parkland DCCs are not yet in force (draft rates only).
flags.correction: They are in force from 24 Jul 2026 (non-residential $5.30 and $0.24/sf; apartments $6,791 and $303/unit) and step to $7.51, $0.60, $9,630 and $763 on 1 Jan 2027.
flags.detail: Metro Vancouver DCC page (S45): Board final adoption 24 Jul 2026; rates apply to building permits issued on or after that date. Raised against the round-1 critique, not the original spec.

flags.claim: Final adopted ACC rates, phase-in and credit rules equal the July 2026 staff proposal.
flags.detail: City summaries seen in search results say Council approved the update on 21 Jul 2026 (S41, S24) and list a 28 Jul by-law item (S42), but Table 1 and by-law text were not opened (HTTP 403); rates come from press summaries.

flags.claim: The CAC policy still targets a minimum of 75% of land lift after the July 2026 update.
flags.detail: The 75% figure is quoted by a secondary blog from policy 1.2(c) as amended October 2025; the primary policy was not opened; Lincoln Institute reports 70-80%; CAC targets are removed for new rezonings, so survival for large projects is unknown.

flags.claim: A price per sf for new downtown condominiums in 2026.
flags.detail: No opened source gives one. Only a marketing blog ($1,100-1,350/sf Yaletown resale one-bedroom) and an unopened page ($1,541/sf new low-rise) exist. The tool uses a user-entered price or a break-even instead of a default.

flags.claim: Current downtown retail net rents.
flags.detail: The latest opened evidence is Colliers via RENX from July 2022 (Robson 1000 block $180-240/sf; 1100 block $75-125/sf). Later figures appear only in unopened search summaries.

flags.claim: CoStar's 2025 Vancouver hotel figures (78.4%, C$284.44 ADR, C$223.05 RevPAR) represent a downtown luxury tower hotel.
flags.detail: CoStar does not define the Vancouver market in the release; annual averages include the summer peak. The Shangri-La Vancouver sale near C$1.0M per room (June 2025) was a share sale with an allocated price reported by Altus Data Studio.

flags.claim: A 4.72% cap rate is suitable for underwriting a downtown tower or its hotel component.
flags.detail: 4.72% is CoStar's Metro-wide office figure (Lee, Q2 2026), not transaction evidence; Lee's average sale $477/sf implies about half the value at 4.72%. CBRE/Colliers cap-rate surveys and hotel cap rates were not opened.

flags.claim: Ahlfeldt and Barr's cost elasticities (about 0.26 commercial, 0.56 residential) hold for Vancouver towers.
flags.detail: Read from the LSE working-paper PDF (introduction about 0.25, section 4.1 says 0.26); the regression design is confirmed (building-level, by floor count); the published version may differ; the global Emporis sample ends below supertall heights.

flags.claim: Altus 2026 Vancouver unit costs, including the C$470/sf Class A office figure attributed to Altus by a secondary blog.
flags.detail: The 2026 guide is gated by a registration form and the blog returned HTTP 404; neither is used.

flags.claim: The VTC brief requires, rather than recommends, at least 9.0 FSR non-residential and states which uses count.
flags.detail: Brief PDF not opened. Listings (S39) say a strong employment component is recommended with a minimum of 9.0 FSR non-residential. Confirm the clause; the Q&A deadline is 3 Nov 2026 (S38).

flags.claim: City-wide DCL ($49.88/m2) and Utilities DCL ($39.06/m2) rates after the 20% reduction hold for this scheme.
flags.detail: A consultancy blog (S50) lists residential-type rates and was written before the Q2 2026 update; commercial rates were not retrieved; the City bulletin returned HTTP 403.

flags.claim: TransLink DCC non-residential rates ($1.16 office, $1.44 retail per sf from 1 Jan 2026) apply in Vancouver.
flags.detail: Read from a City of Langley schedule (S46) with jumbled text columns; assignment inferred from row order and 2024 Burnaby rates; verify against TransLink Bylaw 159-2025.

flags.claim: The ACC is credited against a negotiated CAC, and the ACC deferral works like the DCL deferral.
flags.detail: Press summaries (S23, S43) report credits and a 25% pre-permit deferral; BC guidance (S44) bars Density Bonus for amenities already in an ACC by-law. By-law text not opened.

flags.claim: Downtown annual net absorption history for 5-10 years.
flags.detail: CBRE Figure 2 is a chart without values; Cresa all-class quarterly values (S49) swing about -343,000 to +331,000 sf with alignment uncertain; brokers use different building sets, so the range is a team multiplier on the H1 2026 anchor.

flags.claim: Presale absorption, unsold new-condo inventory and lender presale thresholds for downtown strata.
flags.detail: No opened source; only 11.4% sales-to-listings (S06, secondary). CMHC rents (S05) are existing stock, so a new-build rent row is required.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is the policy that will govern the competition scheme.
flags.detail: The policy review is under way: first-phase engagement results are due early 2027, with draft directions and Council consideration later. The brief itself calls its documents non-legal and says the jury may reward justified breaches. Do not assume new bonus-density rules.

flags.claim: A developer return of 15% of GDV is the minimum acceptable.
flags.detail: Taken from UK PPG para 019 (15-20% of GDV for plan-making), a transferable convention. Vancouver feasibility practice (Coriolis reports for the City) was not opened. Editable.

flags.claim: Preset thresholds: evidence age 6/12 months; break-even rent ratio 1.00/1.15; absorption load 5%/10% of AAA+A building area; 2/4 years to lease; development spread 150/100 bp; probability of feasibility 0.80/0.50; trade-value ratio 1.5/2.0; 26-storey cost anchor.
flags.detail: None has a source; all are editable and displayed as team assumptions, separate from any sourced benchmark.

flags.claim: New r1 presets: absorption multipliers 0.5x/1x/2x; 70/20/10 office/hotel/retail split of the 9.0 FSR; default AACE Class 5; floor-cost profile; blank load factors, TI, LC, free rent and presale rows.
flags.detail: No source; all editable and labelled team assumptions. Blank rows must be entered by the user or left flagged.

flags.claim: Whether cultural, civic and public floors count toward the brief's 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum.
flags.detail: The brief says 'non-residential, high-employment floor area (office, commercial)'. P08-M06 shows both readings until the organisers clarify; the Q&A deadline is 3 Nov 2026.

flags.claim: Current City of Vancouver commercial DCL rates, and whether the 20% reduction applies on top of any rate listed.
flags.detail: City pages returned HTTP 403 again in r1. Metro Vancouver sewer, water and parkland DCCs and the TransLink DCC were retrieved; City commercial DCL and Utilities DCL rates were not.

flags.claim: By-law floor-area exclusions that separate FSR floor area from Layer 0 GFA.
flags.detail: Zoning and Development By-law pages returned HTTP 403; M06 uses editable exclusion rules until the by-law is read.

flags.claim: ACC class and exemption status of hotel and of City-owned or non-profit cultural/civic floors.
flags.detail: The ACC lists 'commercial and other uses' at $3.00/sf; statutory exemptions (S44) do not obviously cover civic or cultural floors; City treatment is not in the opened sources.

flags.claim: Rentable/usable load factors and BOMA 2017 (ANSI/BOMA Z65.1) area definitions, plus the strata saleable-area definition.
flags.detail: The BOMA standard was not opened and the search budget was exhausted; load factors are blank team assumptions until sourced.

unresolved_relationships: Net-to-gross efficiency versus floor-plate area and depth for 244-305 m mixed-use towers: only a qualitative negative correlation with height exists (Ilgin 2025, 166 towers); no sourced slope or plate-size curve.
Core-to-GFA versus lift count, sky lobbies and refuge floors under the Vancouver Building By-law: needs the SYST packet; no sourced curve.
Structural system versus net-to-gross at supertall heights: rigid-frame 85% is height-confounded; the tapered supertall sample found no significant system effect; needs STRC.

Unit hard cost versus height above 39 storeys for Vancouver mixed-use towers: Altus 2026 tables are gated; the only quantified link is the global building-level elasticity (Ahlfeldt and Barr), larger at extreme heights.
Per-use base hard costs for office, hotel, retail, below-grade parking and the below-grade transit connection in Vancouver: no opened source.

Effective rent versus asking rent in downtown Vancouver: BOMA BC reports high tenant incentives (attributed to Cushman & Wakefield) but no magnitude; TI, commissions and free-rent levels are unsourced.

Rent or price premium by floor height in Vancouver: elasticities found (0.03 commercial, 0.07 residential in US cities; 0.086-0.189 within US commercial buildings) are not Vancouver; view premia unknown.
Rentable-to-usable load factor and strata saleable-area definitions linking P08-M02 usable area to rent and price bases (BOMA 2017 not opened).
Zoning and Development By-law floor area (used for FSR) versus Layer 0 GFA: exclusion rules for below-grade, mechanical and amenity space.
Downtown annual net absorption history (5-10 years) and the share a new AAA tower could capture: CBRE Figure 2 has no values; Cresa and CBRE use different building sets.
Presale absorption, unsold new-condo inventory, lender presale threshold and new-build rental rents for downtown Vancouver.
Cap rates for new downtown AAA office, multifamily rental and full-service hotel: investor surveys not opened; 4.72% is a CoStar Metro figure.
Hotel total-revenue ratios (rooms share, departmental costs, management fee, FF&E reserve) and value per key versus RevPAR for luxury tower hotels in Vancouver.
Pass-through of CAC/ACC and public floor area to land price and housing supply: Coriolis 2014/2019 conclusions were not retrieved.
Whether the 75% land-lift target survives for large rezonings after 30 Sep 2026, whether the City nets lift across uses, and how in-kind amenities are valued against the CAC.
Size and rules of the ACC credit against a negotiated CAC, and ACC class of hotel and cultural/civic floors.
Soft-cost %, contingency %, financing carry and construction duration versus height for Vancouver tall towers; cost escalation over a 5-7 year build.
Baseline (as-of-right) entitlement and land value for the hypothetical VTC site, including CBD land-value evidence for a consolidated block; needed for land lift and the land benchmark.
Cost of Vancouver rezoning sustainability requirements (Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, embodied carbon) and Higher Buildings 'excellence' expectations: not retrieved (HTTP 403).
Phasing of multi-tower schemes and its effect on finance, absorption and charges: not modelled in P08-M05a.
Parametric massing rule linking storeys, core and NTG for the P08-M07 density sweep: a team assumption until declared.
change_log: R1 (21 Oct 2026): Defined 8 modules (P08-M01 to M08) covering value by use, floor-plate efficiency, construction cost and tall-building premium, development charges/ACC/CAC, pro forma and residual land value, public-use cost, trade-off explorer and uncertainty engine.

Extracted the CBRE Q2 2026 downtown class table from the PDF (net asking rent, T&O, vacancy by class); a search summary had quoted only the $31.20 metro blended figure, which is now logged as a FALSE ASSUMPTION if used as downtown rent.

Found that Vancouver's city-wide ACC takes effect 30 Sep 2026 and removes CAC targets for new rezonings; legacy-CAC use is logged as a FALSE ASSUMPTION and the ACC rates are marked unverified against the City bulletin (HTTP 403).

Read cost elasticities (about 0.26 commercial, 0.56 residential), the 2%-per-floor rule of thumb and AACE 56R-08 estimate-class ranges from the primary documents; the Altus 2026 Vancouver tables could not be obtained.

The web search budget ran out partway through, so searches for other cost consultants (Cumming, RLB, Turner & Townsend), cap-rate surveys, and current retail rents were not done; these gaps appear in flags and unresolved_relationships.

Library licences verified on repository pages: SALib MIT, numpy-financial BSD-3, IfcOpenShell LGPL-3.0/GPL-3.0, Vega-Lite BSD-3, plotly.js MIT, pymoo Apache-2.0, trimesh MIT, rhino3dm MIT, Shapely BSD-3 (GEOS LGPL-2.1), Speckle Server Apache-2.0; SciPy and the Anthropic xlsx skill were not re-opened.

r1: Removed the dependency cycles by splitting P08-M05 into M05a (RLV before CAC) and M05b (land lift, CAC, RLV after CAC), and by keeping M04 to statutory charges with no link to M05; M07 and M08 are outer wrappers. The critique's 'M04 computes lift' would still loop through M04's charges, so lift moved to M05b. DAG published in notes.

r1: Rewrote the M05a formulas: residual mode RLV = (GDV - TDC excl. land - r x GDV) / (1 + a + f) and profit mode with land at benchmark plus acquisition and land finance; added transfer tax, legal, land carry, disposal and purchaser's costs and GST treatment; added a hand-worked unit-test example (RLV 138.9; profit 150 = 15%).

r1: Separated each threshold's benchmark source from the team cut-off. M02 NTG/core, M05a profit and RLV, and M05b CAC metrics are now team_assumption or unverified; the UK PPG 15% line and the 75% CAC share are logged as FALSE ASSUMPTION when treated as verified. Only the Altus storey band (S13, opened) stays verified.

r1: Corrected the gross-leasing-as-absorption error: absorption now uses H1 2026 downtown net absorption (+103,062 sf; AAA+A rows +128,448, derived from the CBRE table) with 0.5x/1x/2x team multipliers; leasing activity is shown only as deal flow. Logged as FALSE ASSUMPTION.

r1: Corrected the height-elasticity use after re-reading the paper (footnote 16, Fig. 6 note): premium is applied once per building with eps blended by GFA share; floor distribution is a labelled assumption; the stacking-order claim is deleted; added Ahlfeldt and McMillen 2018, the 85% missing-cost caveat and the 1971 date of the 2% rule.
